questions: Does 'subsequence' mean any subsequence (not necessarily contiguous) that is strictly increasing, and we want the maximum possible length among all such subsequences, or just any subsequence length (e.g., the first one found)?
Are we allowed to skip elements arbitrarily in the subsequence, or must we take a contiguous subsequence?
Should the subsequence elements be strictly increasing in value, or strictly increasing in index (i.e., strictly increasing values)?
Is the subsequence required to consist of elements with values at most X_i, or indices at most X_i?
Do we consider the subsequence from the entire prefix up to R_i, or only at positions exactly R_i?
If multiple subsequences satisfy the conditions, should we output the maximum length, minimum length, or any valid length?
Is the subsequence required to be strictly increasing in terms of the order of indices (i.e., we must pick elements in increasing index order)?
Should the output be the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence within the prefix with values ≤ X_i, or just any subsequence length that meets criteria?
